chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you commence the prayer, raise your two palms, then extend them fully, then say Takbir three times, then say: 'O Allah, You are the True King, there is no god but You, Glory be to You, I have wronged myself, so forgive my sin, for no one forgives sins except You.'

Then say Takbir twice, then say: 'Here I am and at Your service, and goodness is in Your hands, and evil is not to You, and the Guided one is the one You guide, there is no refuge from You except to You, Glory be to You, and Your tenderness, Blessed and Exalted, Glory be to You, Lord of the House.'

Then say Takbir twice, then say: 'I turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, upright and Muslim, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my prayer, my rituals, my life, and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, no partner for Him, and by that I was commanded, and I am of the Muslims.'
Then seek refuge from the accursed Satan, then recite the Opening of the Book.

key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and actions for the opening of the prayer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual sequence for the opening of prayer, emphasizing the distinct Shia practice of raising hands multiple times alongside a structured series of Takbirs and supplications. It highlights the theological emphasis on divine sovereignty and forgiveness through the recitation of 'Allāhumma anta al-malik al-ḥaqq', reflecting the Imami tradition of integrating detailed devotional acts with Quranic recitation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim Bin Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you open the Salāt, so raise your palms, then extend them with an extension. Then exclaim three Takbīrs, then say, ‘O Allahazwj! Youazwj are the King, the Truth. There is no god except for Youazwj. Glory be to Youazwj. I have been unjust to myself, therefore Forgive my sins for me, for no one forgives the sins except for Youazwj’.

Then exclaim two Takbīrs, then say, ‘Here I am and at Yourazwj service, and the goodness is in Yourazwj Hands, and the evil is not to Youazwj, and the Guided one is the one whom Youazwj Guide. There is no Shelter (apart) from Youazwj except to Youazwj. Glory be to Youazwj, and Tender are Youazwj, and Blessed, and Exalted. Glory be to Youazwj, Lordazwj of the House!’

Then exclaim two Takbīrs, then you should be saying, ‘I divert my face to the One Who Originated the skies and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, with uprightness and submissiveness, and I am not from the Polytheists. My Salāt, and my rituals, and my life, and my death are for Allahazwj, Lordazwj of the worlds. There is no associate for Youazwj, and by that I am Commanded, and I am from the Muslims’.
Then seek Refuge from the Pelted Satan<sup>la</sup>, then recite the Opening of the Book (Chapter 1)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

as introduction for prayer raise your hands and open them, then say three times, ‘Allah is great and then say, ‘O Lord, You are the true owner. No one other than You deserves to be worshipped. You are free of all defects. I have wronged myself so forgive my sins; no one other than You is able to forgive sins.’

Then say two times, ‘Allah is great.’ Then say, ‘(O Lord), here I am to obey Your command and asking help from You (to accomplish my duty); all good is in Your hands and evil has no way toward You. Guided are those whom You have granted guidance. There is no place of refuge from You (Your anger) except in Your presence. You are free of all defects and compassionate, the most Blessed, the most High. You are free of all defects and You are the Lord of the House.’

Then say two times, ‘Allah is great.’ Then say. ‘I have turned my face toward the One who has created the skies and the earth. He has knowledge of the unseen and seen. I am humble before and submitted to the will of Allah and I am not one of the pagans. My Salah (prayer), my practices, my life and my death are all for the sake of Allah, Cherisher of the worlds. He has no partner. I am commanded to speak as such and I am the first Muslim.’
Then seek refuge with Allah against Satan, who is subject to stoning and then read al-Fatihah.”
